steps.do: Count radio and checkbox inputs in the signup form to size the group.
Wrap each group in a fieldset with class space-y-2 and min-w-0, and give it a legend with text-sm font-medium.
Plan one legend per group so screen readers announce the question before each option.

Check the option target size. Each option row must be 44px tall, which is Tailwind h-11 or min-h-11 (2.75rem at a 16px root). The plan needs at least one match per option, so a count of 0 means the rows are not yet sized to 44px.
Record the fieldset structure in the plan file for the build stage.

K-018752.example: A plan lists a plan-type fieldset with legend text-sm font-medium and 3 radio inputs stacked with space-y-2, and each option row uses h-11 for a 44px target. The rg count shows 3 radio controls in the file, and the target check finds 3 h-11 matches.
K-018752.check: The rg -c command prints the number of radio and checkbox lines. The rg -n command prints one line per 44px option row, so a count matching the option count means the targets are sized. The plan file exists with one fieldset per planned group.
traps: Small models use div instead of fieldset, so the group has no shared name for assistive technology. Use fieldset with legend.
Do not leave min-w-0 off the fieldset, because a long child can overflow the grid column.
A row shorter than 44px fails touch target guidance even when the labels look correct. Check the number, not the appearance.

steps.do: Run the Playwright spec that checks RTL tab order.
Confirm the spec compares bounding box x positions of the first and second tab.
Check the layout sets dir on the html element for the Arabic locale.

K-018753.example: Locale ar sets html dir=rtl, so the first tab has boundingBox x 812 and the second has x 640, meaning the order is reversed left to right. The spec asserts firstTab.x is greater than secondTab.x for the ar locale.
K-018753.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and grep prints a line number for boundingBox in the spec.
traps: Small models check the wrong direction, expecting x to increase in RTL.
Tailwind's rtl: variant needs dir on an ancestor, not a class alone.
Use ms- and me- for margins in RTL, not ml- and mr-.

steps.do: Run the touch target spec on the mobile project.
Confirm the tab button uses the min-h-11 class.
Check the spec asserts a minimum height of 44 pixels.

K-018754.example: The spec reads boundingBox for each role=tab and expects height of at least 44, and the it tab 'Impostazioni account' measures 46px. In Tailwind, min-h-11 sets 2.75rem, which equals 44px at the default 16px root size.
K-018754.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and grep shows min-h-11 with a line number.
traps: Small models write min-h-44, which Tailwind does not provide.
Use min-h-11 for 2.75rem, which is 44px.
Padding alone does not guarantee the rendered box height.

steps.do: Build the app so the static pages exist.
Run axe on the Arabic tabs page.
Run axe on the German tabs page.
Check the text color class used on inactive tabs.

K-018755.example: Inactive tab text text-slate-500 on bg-white measures about 4.8:1, which passes the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text. The text-slate-400 class on white measures about 2.6:1 and fails.
K-018755.check: axe prints 0 violations for color-contrast on each URL, and grep shows the inactive class with a line number.
traps: Small models check only the active tab, but inactive tab text also needs 4.5:1.
Do not use text-slate-400 on white for labels.
The selected underline color is a separate check from the text color.

steps.do: Run the ARIA linkage spec for tabs and panels.
Run the timing spec that measures a tab switch in the browser.
Confirm the panel element uses the tabpanel role.
Run axe on the English tabs page for ARIA rule violations.

K-018756.example: The tab button id tab-profile has aria-controls panel-profile, and the matching tabpanel has aria-labelledby tab-profile. A switch from en to ja completes in 84ms, which is under the 200ms limit in the timing spec.
K-018756.check: Playwright prints '2 passed' across the two specs, and the timing assertion shows elapsed under 200.
traps: Small models set aria-selected but forget aria-controls and tabindex -1 on inactive tabs.
Measure switch time in the browser with a real event, not with a fixed sleep.
Do not make tab id values depend on the locale.

steps.do: Find the file where the table is built in the UI module.
Add highlight_symbol with a two-character text marker followed by a space, such as '* ', on the Table builder.
Confirm the marker is set and the table is drawn with render_stateful_widget and a TableState.
Run the test that renders into a 40 by 10 TestBackend and looks for the marker on the selected row.

K-018757.example: Set highlight_symbol('* ') on the table, then select index 1 in a TableState. The test asserts the buffer row at index 1 begins with '* ' and no other row does.
K-018757.check: cargo test prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed' and the buffer shows the marker only on the selected row.
traps: Relying on background color alone, which disappears under NO_COLOR or on mono terminals.
Forgetting to pass a TableState, so the highlight symbol is never drawn.
Using a marker wider than the first column, which clips the row text.

steps.do: List each Table construction in the UI code.
Add a header call to each Table with a Row of plain text labels.
Confirm each header row has the same count of labels as the widths list.
Run the test that checks the first buffer row contains every header label.

K-018758.example: Build Row::new(vec!['Name','Size','Status']) and pass three Constraint::Length widths of 20, 10 and 12. The test asserts the first buffer line contains 'Name', 'Size' and 'Status' in order.
K-018758.check: cargo test prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed' and the first buffer row reads Name, Size and Status.
traps: Passing three labels but only two widths, which silently drops a column.
Using icons or colors as the only label for a column.
Styling the header so it looks different but still leaves its text empty.

steps.do: Locate where the app reads its theme or style settings.
Make the theme return a plain default style for table cells whenever NO_COLOR is set to any non-empty value.
Run the test suite with NO_COLOR set to confirm the app compiles and its tests still pass.
Run the test that checks no foreground or background color is set on any table cell.

K-018759.example: With NO_COLOR=1 in the environment, the theme returns Style::default() for every row, so each buffer cell reports Color::Reset for foreground. The test loops over all cells in a 40 by 10 TestBackend.
K-018759.check: cargo test prints 'test result: ok' and every cell in the buffer has Reset foreground and background.
traps: Treating NO_COLOR=0 as unset, when the convention counts any non-empty value.
Removing color from the header but leaving body rows colored.
Hardcoding Color::Rgb values that ignore the theme entirely.

steps.do: Check the current terminal width in the shell.
Define a constant that sets the minimum table width to 60 columns.
Filter the column list so only essential columns remain when the area width is under 60.
Run the narrow-width test with a 50-column TestBackend.

K-018760.example: At area width 50, the Notes and Modified columns are dropped and Name and Status stay, with widths summing to at most 50. The test asserts the buffer contains Name and Status but not Notes.
K-018760.check: cargo test prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed' and the rendered buffer contains Name and Status but no Notes.
traps: Choosing column widths whose sum exceeds the area, which clips the last column.
Hiding a column the user needs to identify the row, such as Name.
Checking width only once at startup and not again after a terminal resize.

steps.do: Find the DataTable constructor calls in the app package.
Set cursor_type to 'row' and show_header to True on the DataTable.
Add columns with explicit label strings before any rows are added.
Run the Textual pilot test that presses down once and checks the cursor row index.

K-018761.example: Create DataTable(cursor_type='row', show_header=True), then add_columns('Name', 'Status'). After pilot.press('down'), the test asserts table.cursor_row equals 1.
K-018761.check: pytest prints '1 passed' and table.cursor_row equals 1 after one down press.
traps: Leaving cursor_type at cell, so row focus is never announced as a row.
Adding rows before columns, which misaligns the labels under the data.
Forgetting to await pilot.press inside the async test, so the cursor never moves.

steps.do: Find where the frame draws the table with its selected index.
After drawing the table, call set_cursor_position with the table's left x and the y of the selected data row.
Run the test that moves the selection to row 2 and reads the cursor position from the TestBackend.

K-018762.check: cargo test prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed' and the TestBackend cursor position is (2, 7).

Forgetting the header line in the y offset, which puts the cursor one row too high.
Moving the cursor before the table is drawn, so the position refers to the previous frame.

steps.do: Count the dark appearance entries in the tint color set.

Confirm the test asserted that the light and dark resolved colors are not equal.

Compare the file count to the expected total of eight images.

steps.do: List the dark entries of the label color set to find its RGB values.
Run the contrast test that computes WCAG ratios for labels against the bar background.
Confirm the test asserts a minimum ratio of 4.5:1 for every unselected tab label.

K-018766.check: xcodebuild ends with ** TEST SUCCEEDED **; a ratio below 4.5:1 prints a failure line naming the label.
traps: Using light-mode colors to judge dark-mode contrast gives the wrong answer. Checking only the selected tab skips the labels most likely to fail. Applying the 3:1 large-text threshold to body text is …

steps.do: Run the performance test that switches between four tabs in dark mode.
Check the reported average switch time for each tap.
Confirm the test asserts an elapsed time below 0.2 seconds for each switch.

K-018767.example: Each tap on the Settings tab averages 0.14 seconds in dark mode. The assertion XCTAssertLessThan(elapsed, 0.2) fails any switch at or above 200ms.
K-018767.check: The log shows an average under 0.2 seconds and xcodebuild ends with ** TEST SUCCEEDED **.
traps: Measuring while another build runs in the simulator skews the numbers. Reporting the total time for all tabs hides a slow individual switch. Comparing seconds against a millisecond threshold gives a …

steps.do: Count the tap-target assertions in the UI test file.
Run the tap-target UI test in dark appearance.
Confirm each tab button frame has a height and width of at least 44 points.

K-018768.example: Four tab buttons each measure 49 points tall and 95 points wide. The grep prints 8 because each button checks both height and width.
K-018768.check: grep prints 8 and xcodebuild ends with ** TEST SUCCEEDED **.

steps.do: Run the overflow spec at a 320px viewport.
Confirm the tablist is a horizontal scroll container.
Check the spec asserts an exact count of clipped tabs.

K-018769.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and grep prints a line number for toHaveCount(0).

Hidden overflow clips text silently, so check each tab.
Whitespace-nowrap without a scroll container still overflows the viewport.

Run the key checker across every locale file.
Count the keys under the tabs block in the Arabic locale.
Count the keys under the tabs block in English for comparison.

An empty string value passes a key-exists check while still showing blank text.
Compare counts for every locale, not two.

Find textScaleFactor uses that should move to textScaler.
Set the golden matrix to 360x640 logical pixels at text scales 1.0 and 2.0 for the locales en, ar, and de.
Check which onboarding test files already exist.
Set body text contrast to at least 4.5:1 and tap targets to at least 48 logical pixels.

K-018771.check: The grep for textScaleFactor prints nothing and exits with status 1, and after goldens exist, find lists 6 PNG files for each onboarding page.

Open tailwind.config.js and add require('@tailwindcss/forms') to the plugins array.
Confirm the content array scans the onboarding source files.
Rebuild the stylesheet with the Tailwind CLI.
Count the lines in the built CSS that contain the forms plugin's appearance rule.

Place the error paragraph directly after the input with classes hidden text-sm text-red-700 peer-invalid:block.
Run the component test that types an invalid email and checks the error text.
Check that the component compiles with no type errors.

K-018773.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the paragraph is hidden on an empty field and visible after typing 'abc'.
traps: Putting peer on the paragraph instead of the input, so the message never appears.
Placing the message before the input, since peer-* variants only style later siblings.
Leaving out required or type email, so the browser never marks the field invalid.

steps.do: Set aria-invalid to the exact string 'true' on the input when its validation fails.
Add classes border-gray-300 aria-[invalid=true]:border-red-600 aria-[invalid=true]:ring-1 aria-[invalid=true]:ring-red-600 to the input.
Rebuild the stylesheet so the aria variant classes are generated.
Run axe against the onboarding profile page and count violations.

K-018774.check: grep -c invalid ./dist/styles.css prints 1 or higher, and axe reports 0 violations.

Using the bare aria-invalid: variant in an older v3 project where it may be missing; use aria-[invalid=true]: instead.
Showing the error only with red color and no text or icon, so color is the only cue.

Give each clickable step the classes focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-indigo-600.
Color the active step circle bg-indigo-600 text-white and the inactive ones bg-gray-200 text-gray-700.
Run axe against the steps page and count violations.
Run the test that tabs to step 3 and checks the ring.

K-018775.check: axe reports 0 violations and Playwright prints '1 passed'.

Picking a ring color close to the background, so the focus ring is nearly invisible.
Marking the active step only with color and no aria-current.

Add classes disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-indigo-600 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 to the button.

Check that the component file matches the Prettier style.

K-018776.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' with a height of 44px, and Prettier prints 'All matched files use Prettier code style!'

steps.do: Find every ul or ol element in the source tree.
Locate the Tailwind config file or the CSS entry file.
Count how many list elements each file contains.
Create the docs folder for the plan file.
Record the default widths: base under 640px, sm at 640px, md at 768px, lg at 1024px, unless the config overrides them.
Confirm the plan file exists and is not empty.

K-018777.example: ProductList.tsx has 2 ul or ol matches and ReviewList.tsx has 1, so there are 3 lists total. The plan maps ProductList to grid-cols-1 at base, sm:grid-cols-2 at 640px, and lg:grid-cols-4 at 1024px.
K-018777.check: rg -c prints src/components/ProductList.tsx:2 and src/components/ReviewList.tsx:1, and test -s exits 0 with no output.

steps.do: List the li elements and their child containers in the list components.
Check for any existing flex-row class that is not behind a prefix.
Write the plan: base uses flex-col gap-3, and md uses md:flex-row md:items-center.
Note that md means 768px, so the row layout starts at that width.
Check that the planned md:flex-row class is recorded in the plan file.

K-018778.example: Each li in OrderList.tsx uses flex-col gap-3 at base and switches to md:flex-row md:items-center at 768px. Below 768px the title sits above the button, and at 768px and wider they share one row.
K-018778.check: rg -n 'md:flex-row' docs/list-responsive-plan.md prints one line containing the planned class.

steps.do: Find existing row classes that set padding or minimum height.
Find the button and link elements inside list rows.
Plan min-h-11 on each row, which Tailwind sets to 2.75rem or 44px.
Plan py-2 and px-3 on each action so its hit area stays at least 44px tall.
Confirm the plan file lists 44px as the minimum tap size.

K-018779.example: Each row in CartList.tsx gets min-h-11 so its height is 44px, and the Remove button uses px-3 py-2. The plan file records 44px as the minimum tap size for every row action.
K-018779.check: rg -n '44px' docs/list-responsive-plan.md prints a line containing 44px.

Do not use min-h-10, which is 40px. Use min-h-11, which is 44px.

steps.do: Find metadata fields such as updatedAt in the list components.
Check whether any metadata already uses the hidden class.
Plan hidden md:block on each metadata span.
Plan keeping the title and primary action visible at every width.
Confirm the plan names the md breakpoint as 768px.

K-018780.check: rg -n 'md:block' docs/list-responsive-plan.md prints one line naming the updatedAt span.

Use the Tailwind hidden and md:block classes, not custom display rules in a separate CSS file.

steps.do: Find the existing Playwright config file.
Check the Playwright version installed in the project.
Write the test widths: 320, 390, 639, 640, 767, 768, 1023, 1024, and 1280 pixels.

Plan one check per width that counts visible rows and confirms the list has role list.
Plan an accessibility scan at each width with the axe CLI.

K-018781.example: The plan for ProductList.tsx tests widths 320px, 639px, 640px, 767px, 768px, and 1024px. Each width runs a Playwright check that the grid has 1 column below 640px and 2 columns at 640px.
K-018781.check: npx playwright --version prints a version such as Version 1.x, and find lists playwright.config.ts or prints nothing if the file is missing.

steps.do: Confirm flutter_localizations is declared in pubspec.yaml.
Read l10n.yaml to confirm the ARB folder and the template file.
List the ARB files that already exist.
Choose the locale list, with en as the template and ar and de as the first translations, and write one app_<code>.arb file for each.

steps.do: Measure the character length of each English onboarding string in the template ARB file.
Record the longest English length as the base.
Multiply the base by 1.3 and round up to set the German budget.
Measure the German onboarding strings against that budget.
Run the button size test that asserts the primary onboarding button keeps a minimum height of 48 logical pixels.

steps.do: List left-side padding values that must become directional.
List hard-coded left and right alignments.
Write the replacement for each match: EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start: ...) and AlignmentDirectional.centerStart.
Confirm no left or right padding values remain after the change.

steps.do: Find every Dart string interpolation in the onboarding folder.
Count the interpolations that need ARB placeholders.
Mark each count-based string as a plural in its ARB entry using ICU syntax.
Declare each placeholder type in its @key block, using int for counts and String for names.
Regenerate the localization classes to check that the placeholders compile.
Run the plural test that asserts Arabic shows all six plural forms for a count placeholder.

K-018785.example: The string 'Step ${current} of ${total}' becomes a placeholder block with current and total typed as int. After flutter gen-l10n, app_localizations.dart contains String onboardingProgress(int current, int total).
K-018785.check: The grep count matches the number of planned placeholders, flutter gen-l10n finishes with no errors and the generated file contains onboardingProgress(int current, int total), and flutter test prints 'All tests passed!' for the six Arabic plural forms.

steps.do: Render the summary above the form with role='alert' and text that counts the invalid fields.
Style the summary with text-sm font-medium text-red-700 bg-red-50 border border-red-200.
Link each summary item to its field with an anchor whose href is the field id.
Run axe on the review page limited to WCAG 2.1 AA rules and count violations.
