K-018819.check: rg prints a line with unicode-width, and cargo test prints 'test button_min_size_12x3 ... ok'.
traps: Using label.len() counts bytes, not display cells, so wide characters break the width.
Clamping to the minimum without intersecting with the parent area draws outside the screen.
Setting height to 1 leaves no row for the focus marker or border.

steps.do: In src/app.rs, match KeyCode::Enter and KeyCode::Char(' ') in the key handler, and only act when this button has focus.
Call the button's on_press callback once per key press, and ignore events whose kind is Release.
Confirm the Enter key arm exists in the handler.
Run the test that sends a Space key event and asserts the save counter goes from 0 to 1.

K-018820.example: When the Save button has focus, pressing Enter increments the save count from 0 to 1 once. Pressing Space does the same, and pressing Tab moves focus away without firing.
K-018820.check: rg prints the line with KeyCode::Enter, and cargo test prints 'test button_space_activates ... ok' followed by 'test result: ok. 1 passed'.
traps: Firing on the Release event as well as Press makes some terminals activate the button twice.
Handling Enter globally instead of only when focused triggers the wrong button.
Matching Space as a string instead of KeyCode::Char(' ') means the arm never runs.

steps.do: Add a disabled bool field to Button and append the text (disabled) to the label when it is true.
In the focus-order list, exclude buttons where disabled is true so Tab skips them.
Confirm the disabled suffix is in the render code.
Run the test that presses Tab across three buttons and asserts the disabled middle one is skipped.

K-018821.example: A Button labelled Submit with disabled set to true renders as [ Submit (disabled) ], and Tab moves focus from Cancel straight to Help.
K-018821.check: rg prints the render line containing (disabled), and cargo test prints 'test button_disabled_skipped_by_tab ... ok' followed by 'test result: ok. 1 passed'.
traps: Dimming the colour alone tells a colour-blind or no-colour user nothing.
Keeping disabled buttons in the focus list lets focus land on something that cannot fire.
Leaving the parentheses unquoted in the rg pattern makes the shell misread the search.

steps.do: Create tests/button_snapshot.rs and import ratatui::backend::TestBackend and ratatui::Terminal.
Build a Terminal over TestBackend::new(12, 3), draw the Button with label OK, and read the buffer.
Count the test files that mention TestBackend to confirm the test file exists.
Run the snapshot test and check that row 1 of the buffer contains the text OK.

K-018822.example: Drawing Button OK into TestBackend::new(12, 3) puts the text OK somewhere on row 1. The test asserts that row 1 contains OK and does not assert the full buffer, so border changes do not break it.
K-018822.check: rg -c prints 1, and cargo test prints 'test button_snapshot ... ok' followed by 'test result: ok. 1 passed'.
traps: Asserting the whole buffer equals a string breaks on any border change; check the label row only.
Using a backend smaller than the minimum size from the size card makes the button skip drawing.
Searching the wrong directory makes rg -c print 0, so confirm the tests path first.

steps.do: Build the site so each locale gets its own static page.
Confirm the Arabic page sets lang and dir on the html element.
Run the browser test that asserts document.dir for each locale.
Confirm the English page still declares dir ltr on the html element.

K-018823.example: The Arabic build line reads html lang=ar dir=rtl, and the English build line reads html lang=en dir=ltr. The Playwright test then prints 1 passed for the Arabic locale and 1 passed for the English locale.
K-018823.check: grep prints one html line per page with the expected lang and dir values, and Playwright prints 2 passed with no failures.
traps: Setting dir only on body leaves the html element wrong for some checks. Set it on the html element.
Do not hardcode dir=rtl in the shared template, because every locale then inherits it. Set it from the locale value.

steps.do: Search the stylesheets for physical left and right properties.
Replace each hit with margin-inline-start, padding-inline-end, or text-align: start.
Re-run the same search and expect no output.
Run the layout test that checks the nav bar mirrors in RTL.

K-018824.example: The search first prints src/styles/nav.css:14 margin-left: 1rem, and after the edit it becomes margin-inline-start: 1rem. The second search prints nothing and the Playwright test prints 1 passed.
K-018824.check: The final grep prints no lines and exits with status 1, and the Playwright run reports 1 passed.
traps: Mapping margin-left to margin-right by hand breaks LTR. Use margin-inline-start so the value follows dir.
Physical float and text-align values are easy to miss in inline style attributes. Search the HTML files too.

steps.do: Build the German locale so its strings load.
Run the overflow test for navigation labels.
Confirm the test lengthens each German label by 1.3 times its English length before measuring.

K-018825.example: The label Einstellungen und Datenschutz sits in a 180px nav item, and its scrollWidth must not exceed clientWidth. Playwright prints 1 passed when the label fits.
K-018825.check: The Playwright run prints a passed line with 0 failed, and each nav item has scrollWidth no greater than clientWidth.
traps: A fixed px width clips longer words, so use min-width and flex-wrap: wrap instead.
Testing only English strings hides expansion, so run the German build.

steps.do: Find components that render user-supplied text.
Add the dir=auto attribute to each element that shows user text.
Confirm the attribute is present in the user name component.
Run the bidi isolation test on a mixed Arabic and Latin name.

K-018826.example: A span holding the name محمد Smith with dir=auto reports computed direction rtl for its first strong character. The surrounding paragraph keeps dir ltr, and Playwright prints 1 passed.
K-018826.check: grep prints the user-name.html line containing dir=auto, and Playwright prints 1 passed with 0 failed.
traps: Adding dir=auto to the whole page instead of user text changes the layout for everyone. Apply it only to user-content elements.
dir=auto picks direction from the first strong character, so test a name that starts with Latin text too.

steps.do: Create a folder for the Lighthouse reports.
Run Lighthouse accessibility audit on the Arabic page and write JSON output.
Run the same Lighthouse audit on the English page.
Read the Arabic accessibility score from the JSON report.
Confirm both scores are at least 0.9 on the 0 to 1 scale.

K-018827.example: The jq output for reports/ar.json prints 1, and the jq output for reports/en.json also prints 1. Both values sit above the 0.9 threshold.
K-018827.check: jq prints a number from 0 to 1 for each report, and both values are 0.9 or higher.
traps: Lighthouse scores run from 0 to 1, not 0 to 100, so 95 means a failure to read. Compare against 0.9.
The server from the axe card must be running, or Lighthouse reports an unreachable URL.

steps.do: Install the axe helper for the Playwright suite.
Start the built app on port 4173 and keep it running.
Run the contrast spec that scans the tabs page in light and dark themes with axe.
Count color-contrast violations in the Playwright output folder.
Confirm each theme's tab label meets 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

K-018828.example: The light tab label #767676 on #ffffff measures 4.54:1, and the dark tab label #a0a0a0 on #121212 measures 7.2:1. Both pass the 4.5:1 threshold, so the axe scan should report zero color-contrast violations.
K-018828.check: The Playwright run prints "1 passed", and rg -c finds no matches, so it exits with status 1 and prints nothing.
traps: Scanning only the light theme misses the dark failures.
Setting the dark class after axe runs means the scan never sees dark colors.
Treating a 4.5:1 label on a hover color as passing without checking the hover state.

steps.do: Install Vue Test Utils, jsdom, and Vitest as dev dependencies.
Write the spec that mounts AppTabs.vue and clicks the theme toggle button.
Run the Vitest spec for the tabs and the theme toggle.
Re-run the same spec with the verbose reporter to list each test by name.
Confirm the active tab still has aria-selected set to true after the toggle.

K-018829.example: After trigger('click') on the .theme-toggle button and await nextTick(), document.documentElement.classList contains "dark" and the first role="tab" element has aria-selected="true". The test asserts both values.
K-018829.check: Vitest prints "Tests 3 passed (3)" with no failed lines.
traps: Checking the class on wrapper.element instead of document.documentElement, where the dark class actually lives.
Skipping await nextTick() after trigger, so the assertions read the old DOM.
Running Vitest without environment jsdom in vitest.config.ts, which breaks the document lookup.

steps.do: Run the keyboard spec that presses ArrowRight across the tab list in the dark theme.
Read the computed outline width and color of the focused role="tab" element in the spec.
Confirm the focus outline color meets 3:1 against the adjacent dark background.
Re-run the keyboard spec filtered to the light theme.

K-018830.example: Pressing ArrowRight on the first tab moves focus to the second tab and sets its aria-selected to true. The focus outline is 2px solid #3b9eff on #121212, which measures 6.7:1 and passes the 3:1 non-text threshold.
K-018830.check: Both Playwright runs print "passed", and the spec asserts outlineWidth equals "2px" with no failures.
traps: Checking focus on the wrapper div instead of the role="tab" button element.
Testing only one theme, so a dark-only low-contrast ring goes unnoticed.
Forgetting that ArrowRight on the last tab should wrap to the first tab, and not testing it.

steps.do: Create the spec that calls page.emulateMedia with colorScheme set to dark, then set it to light.
Clear localStorage in beforeEach so a saved manual theme cannot override the OS setting.
Run the OS theme spec for the tabs page.
List the spec names to confirm there is one test per color scheme.

K-018831.example: Calling page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' }) and reloading the page should set the html data-theme attribute to "dark" within 200ms. The light case should set it to "light" the same way.
K-018831.check: The --list run shows exactly 2 tests, and the full run prints "2 passed".
traps: Leaving a saved localStorage theme in place, which hides the OS setting and makes the test pass for the wrong reason.
Reading data-theme before the page finishes its mount, so the assertion runs too early.
Testing only dark, which misses a light regression.

steps.do: Run vue-tsc to type-check the components and the theme composable.
Run eslint on the tabs component and the theme composable.
Run eslint again with zero allowed warnings to make the check strict.
Confirm the theme prop type is the union 'light' | 'dark' and nothing wider.

K-018832.example: If the theme prop is typed as 'light' | 'dark' and a caller passes 'blue', vue-tsc reports TS2322 and exits with status 2. A clean run exits 0 with no output.
K-018832.check: vue-tsc prints nothing and exits 0, and the eslint run prints "0 problems".
traps: Typing the theme prop as string, which accepts any value and hides the mistake.
Ignoring vue-tsc output because the dev server still runs.
Counting warnings as acceptable when the project expects zero.

steps.do: Find the line number of the inline theme script in index.html.
Confirm that line number is smaller than the line of the module script tag in index.html.
Run the no-flash spec that reads the html class right after DOMContentLoaded.
Confirm the spec asserts the dark class appears within 200ms of DOMContentLoaded.

K-018833.example: The inline script on line 8 of index.html reads localStorage key "theme" and sets the dark class on the html element. The spec measures the class at 12ms after DOMContentLoaded, well under the 200ms limit.
K-018833.check: rg shows the theme script line number lower than the module script line, and the Playwright run prints "1 passed".
traps: Putting the theme script after the module script, which causes a visible flash of light theme.
Matching unrelated lines with rg -n theme, such as CSS comments, and reading the wrong line.
Checking the class only after the app mounts, which misses the flash entirely.

steps.do: In App startup, read std::env::var_os NO_COLOR and store a bool no_color set only when the value is non-empty.
In Button::render, skip fg and bg colours when no_color is true, and keep modifiers such as REVERSED and BOLD.
Search the source for the environment read to confirm it exists in the startup path.
Run the colour-free test with NO_COLOR set to 1, then check that the summary reports exactly 1 passed and 0 failed.

K-018834.example: With NO_COLOR=1 set, a focused Button labelled Exit renders with REVERSED and no Color::Red foreground. Without the variable, the same button uses Color::Red.
K-018834.check: rg prints the environment read line in the startup code. The cargo test summary line reads 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed', and the test line reads 'test button_no_color ... ok'.
traps: Checking NO_COLOR only in the test and not in the real startup path hides the bug.
The convention ignores an empty NO_COLOR, so check that the value is non-empty, not only that it exists.
Removing modifiers along with colours removes the focus cue.

steps.do: In terminal 1, serve the dist folder on port 8080. This command runs in the foreground, so leave it running for the remaining steps.
In terminal 2, confirm the Arabic page responds with status 200.
Run axe against the Arabic page at the WCAG 2 AA tag.
Run only the color-contrast rule. The run must report 0 violations, which means each text color meets at least 4.5:1 against its background.
Stop the server by pressing Ctrl-C in terminal 1, then confirm the port no longer responds.

K-018835.example: The curl response shows HTTP/1.0 200 OK, and axe reports 0 violations for the Arabic page. The text color #767676 on #ffffff measures 4.54:1, which passes the 4.5:1 minimum. After Ctrl-C, curl reports connection refused.
K-018835.check: curl prints a 200 status line, axe prints 0 violations with the lang attribute check passing, the color-contrast run prints 0 violations, and the final curl fails with connection refused.
traps: axe does not detect a missing dir attribute, so check dir separately.
Stopping the server before running axe causes connection errors, so keep the server running in terminal 1 during the test.

steps.do: Open src/components/GridRows.vue and find the v-for that renders each row.
Add v-memo to the row element with a dependency array holding row.id, row.version, and a selection flag.
Confirm each memoized element has a stable :key set to row.id.
Run the type checker to confirm the template still compiles.
Run the spec that counts row renders after one row changes.

K-018836.example: <tr v-for='row in rows' :key='row.id' v-memo='[row.id, row.version, row.id === selectedId]'> skips 999 unchanged rows when only row 42 changes. The spec then reports 1 row render instead of 1000.
K-018836.check: vitest prints 'Tests 1 passed' and the render-count assertion shows 1 re-rendered row out of 1000.
traps: Leaving out a value the row template reads makes stale data appear, so list every value the row uses.
Using v-memo without a stable key breaks row reuse when rows are reordered.

steps.do: Create src/components/SidebarPanel.vue containing the heavy panel markup and logic.
In the layout file, replace the static import with defineAsyncComponent that calls import on SidebarPanel.vue.
Set delay to 200 in the options so the loading state only shows for slow loads.
Build the production bundle.
List the built asset sizes to find the separate panel chunk.

K-018837.example: const SidebarPanel = defineAsyncComponent({ loader: () => import('./SidebarPanel.vue'), delay: 200 }) moves about 90KB of panel code into its own chunk. The main index JS then drops from 240KB to 150KB or less.
K-018837.check: ls -l shows a SidebarPanel chunk file, and the index-*.js file is 150KB or smaller.
traps: A static import at the top of the layout file keeps the panel in the main bundle, so remove it.
Defining the async component inside render makes Vue reload it on every render, so define it once at module scope.

steps.do: Open src/stores/layoutTree.ts and change the ref holding the node array to shallowRef.
Update the tree by assigning a new array to .value instead of pushing into the existing array.
Type-check the store file to confirm the shallowRef types are correct.
Create a bench that replaces a tree of 5000 nodes and times the update.
Run the bench in run mode to get the timing for the update.

K-018838.example: const nodes = shallowRef([]) then nodes.value = buildTree(5000) replaces the tree in one assignment. The bench reports the update at 40ms or less, down from 180ms with deep ref.
K-018838.check: The bench output lists the replace-tree median at 50ms or less and vue-tsc exits with no errors.
traps: Mutating nodes.value[0].label does not trigger updates with shallowRef, so replace the array or use triggerRef after an in-place change.
Do not wrap a whole tree in shallowRef when child fields are edited one at a time.

steps.do: Create src/composables/useColumnCount.ts that exports a function taking a template ref and a minimum column width.
Inside the function, create a ResizeObserver in onMounted and schedule updates with requestAnimationFrame.
Call disconnect on the observer in onBeforeUnmount.
Lint the composable file for unused variables and missing cleanup.
Run the composable test that checks disconnect runs once on unmount.

K-018839.example: const columns = useColumnCount(gridRef, 240) reads the container width and returns Math.floor(width / 240) with at least 1. After unmount the test sees disconnect called 1 time.
K-018839.check: eslint prints 0 problems and vitest prints 'Tests 2 passed' with disconnect called exactly once.
traps: Reading clientWidth during render instead of through the observer forces a layout on every update.
Forgetting disconnect leaves observers running after the grid is removed.

steps.do: Open src/layouts/TabLayout.vue and wrap the dynamic component in KeepAlive with max set to 3.
Add onActivated and onDeactivated hooks to the tab panel to pause and resume timers.
Write a Playwright test that switches through the three tabs five times and counts mounted panels.
Run the tab test with Playwright.
Run the type checker to confirm the KeepAlive props type-check.

K-018840.example: <KeepAlive :max='3'><component :is='activeTab' /></KeepAlive> keeps all 3 tab panels in memory after switching. The test shows the mounted hook running 3 times across 15 switches, not 15.
K-018840.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' and the mount counter shows exactly 3 after 15 switches.
traps: Leaving out max lets the cache grow without limit when many tabs are opened.
Using onMounted for work that should pause on deactivate leaves timers running in hidden tabs.

steps.do: Confirm the project uses Vue 3.5 or later so useId is available.
Search for existing useId calls to match the project style.
Plan the error element with an id from useId, role set to alert, and aria-invalid set to true only when error is non-empty.
Run axe against the page that hosts the input once it is built.

K-018841.example: The input gets aria-invalid set to true when error is non-empty, and aria-describedby pointing at an id built from useId plus the suffix -error. The error paragraph has role alert and renders only when error is non-empty.
K-018841.check: npm ls vue prints a vue@3.5 or later line, and axe reports 0 violations for the input.
traps: Setting aria-invalid to false on valid fields adds nothing; omit the attribute instead.
Putting role alert on an always-rendered element makes screen readers announce it on every change; render it only when there is an error.

steps.do: Search for existing debounce helpers or timers to reuse.
Check for existing setTimeout calls in the source tree.
Record a 300ms validation debounce after the last keystroke and a 200ms minimum time that an error stays visible in the plan.
Run the input spec to confirm the timing tests exist and pass once built.

K-018842.example: A watch on the value schedules validation 300ms after the last keystroke, using useDebounceFn from @vueuse/core if the project already has it. Once an error appears it stays for at least 200ms even if the value becomes valid.
K-018842.check: The spec output lists a test named for debounce and a test named for minimum display, and both pass.
traps: Vue has no built-in debounce option on watch; a small model may invent one. Use setTimeout or a debounce helper.
Clearing the error on every keystroke makes it flicker; plan the 200ms floor explicitly.

steps.do: Search the stylesheets for existing error colour tokens to reuse.
Record error text colour #B00020 on a #FFFFFF background, which has a contrast of about 7.3:1 and passes the 4.5:1 minimum.
Check whether existing buttons already use a 44px minimum size.
Run an automated WCAG AA contrast check on the rendered form once it is built.

K-018843.example: The error paragraph uses color #B00020 on a white field, about 7.3:1, and the clear button has min-height 44px and min-width 44px. The plan fixes these values so the styling step has no guesswork.
K-018843.check: axe reports 0 color-contrast violations, and grep finds min-height: 44px on the button rule.
traps: Small models often pick a light red such as #FF6666 that fails 4.5:1 on white. Compute or check the ratio before choosing.
A 24px icon button fails the 44px target; size the hit area, not just the icon.

steps.do: Check that Vitest and Vue Test Utils are installed.
List four test cases in the plan: default has no error, empty shows after blur, error prop renders with aria-invalid true, and error clears when a valid value is set.
Run the type checker on Vue single-file components so typed props are verified.
Run the spec file and confirm the four planned tests are picked up.

K-018844.example: The spec file BaseInput.spec.ts mounts the component with @vue/test-utils mount and asserts the four cases, with flushPromises after each blur. The planned count of 4 is the number the runner must report.
K-018844.check: vitest prints Tests 4 passed (4), and vue-tsc exits with no output.
traps: Small models skip await nextTick or flushPromises after a prop change, so assertions read stale DOM.
Test the error element text and aria-invalid attribute, not only the prop value.

steps.do: Serve the project folder on port 8080 with Python's static server in a separate terminal.
Open the modal page in light mode and run axe with the WCAG 2 AA tag set.
Add data-theme="dark" to the html element and open the dialog, since axe must check the modal while it is open.
Rerun axe on the same page in dark mode and require at least 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text or UI.

K-018845.example: In dark mode the body text is #e6e6e6 on #1e1e24, a ratio of about 13:1, so axe reports no violation. The close button label #8a8a94 on #1e1e24 gives about 4.6:1 and passes the 4.5:1 rule.
K-018845.check: Each axe run exits with code 0 and prints no color-contrast entry under violations, in both light and dark mode.
traps: Small models test only the light theme and stop. Run both themes before calling it verified.
A ratio of 4.4:1 fails the 4.5:1 rule for body text even though it looks close. Compute the number instead of judging by eye.
Axe checks only what is rendered, so open the dialog with showModal first or the modal text is never tested.

steps.do: Create the tests folder if it does not exist.
Write tests/modal-dark.spec.js that calls page.emulateMedia with colorScheme set to dark right after page.goto, then opens the dialog.
In the same spec, call page.evaluate with getComputedStyle on the dialog to read its background-color and color values.
Parse the rgb() numbers, compute the WCAG contrast ratio from relative luminance, and expect the result to be at least 4.5.
Run the spec with Playwright.

K-018846.example: The spec emulates dark mode and reads the dialog as rgb(230, 230, 234) text on rgb(30, 30, 36), a ratio of about 13.1. The expect on 4.5 passes and the run reports 1 passed.
K-018846.check: The output ends with "1 passed" and no expect failure appears for the ratio check.
traps: emulateMedia must run before the dialog opens, or the light palette may already be applied. Call it right after page.goto.
getComputedStyle returns rgb() strings, not hex, so parse the numbers before computing luminance. A parsing mistake gives a false pass.

steps.do: Create the reports folder for the audit output.
Run Lighthouse on modal.html for the accessibility category only and write the JSON to reports/modal-a11y.json.
Confirm the report file exists.
Count how many times the color-contrast audit id appears in the report.

K-018847.example: Lighthouse writes reports/modal-a11y.json with an accessibility score of 1 for modal.html. The grep count for color-contrast is 2, which shows the audit ran and was included.
K-018847.check: test exits with code 0, and the report contains the accessibility category with a score of 1.
traps: Lighthouse's default run covers every category, which is slow. Use --only-categories=accessibility.
A score of 0.92 is not a pass for a release gate. Read the number in the file rather than assuming it is fine.

steps.do: Create the focus spec file in the tests folder.
In the spec, emulate dark color scheme, open the dialog, and press Tab until the close button has focus.
Read the computed outline-color and outline-width of the focused button, and compute its contrast against the dialog background.
Expect the contrast to be at least 3:1 for non-text UI and outline-width to be at least 2px.
Run the spec with Playwright.

K-018848.example: The focused close button has outline-color rgb(138, 180, 255) and outline-width 2px on a background of rgb(30, 30, 36). The ratio is about 7.6:1, so the expects pass and the run reports 1 passed.
K-018848.check: The output reports 1 passed and the contrast and width expects do not fail.
traps: outline: none in modal.css removes the focus ring entirely. Check the computed outline-style is not none.
WCAG non-text contrast is 3:1, not 4.5:1, so do not fail a valid focus ring for missing the body-text bar.

steps.do: Count ::backdrop rules in modal.css to confirm the overlay is styled.
Read the rgba values in modal.css to confirm the dark-mode backdrop alpha is at least 0.6.
In tests/modal-theme.spec.js, run once in light and once in dark, open the dialog with showModal, press Escape, and expect the dialog to be closed within 200ms.
Run the theme spec with the list reporter.

K-018849.example: modal.css has 2 ::backdrop matches, and the dark backdrop is rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7). The spec opens and closes the dialog in both themes, and each close finishes in about 40ms, so the run reports 2 passed.
K-018849.check: The backdrop count is at least 1, the dark alpha is 0.6 or higher, and the run reports 2 passed with no timeout.
traps: ::backdrop applies only to a dialog in the top layer. A div overlay needs its own selector and its own Escape keydown listener.
Testing only one theme can hide a backdrop that is invisible in dark mode. Run both themes.

steps.do: In the section component, add a scoped style rule with content-visibility set to auto on the section root class.
Set contain-intrinsic-size to auto 600px so the scroll height stays stable before rendering.
Build the production bundle.
In a separate terminal, start the preview server on port 4173 and leave it running.
Run Lighthouse against the preview server and write the results to a JSON file.
Read the cumulative layout shift value from lh.json and confirm it is below 0.1.
Read the largest contentful paint value from lh.json and confirm it is below 2500.

K-018850.example: .section-card { content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 600px; } applies to 12 sections below the fold. Lighthouse then reports rendering work for only the 2 visible sections at load.
K-018850.check: lh.json shows cumulative-layout-shift numericValue below 0.1 and largest-contentful-paint numericValue below 2500.
traps: Setting content-visibility without contain-intrinsic-size makes the page jump as sections load in, so always set a size.
Applying it to elements that hold focus or are needed for find-in-page can hide content from the user.

steps.do: List all Vue files whose names contain Input.
Search the components folder for files that already mention error.
Count how many times modelValue appears in each component file.
Run the existing component tests to get a baseline pass count before any change.
Write the chosen component path, the candidate file count from find, and the passed test count into the plan.

K-018851.example: find prints src/components/BaseInput.vue and src/components/forms/TextField.vue, so there are 2 candidates. grep -rc shows modelValue in 2 files. vitest reports 14 passed and 0 failed. The plan reuses BaseInput.vue by adding an error prop and records the numbers 2, 2, and 14.
K-018851.check: find prints at least one path ending in .vue, and vitest prints a passed count with 0 failed. If find prints nothing, the plan must create BaseInput.vue from scratch, say so, and record 0 candidates.
traps: Small models often create a new component when one already exists, so list files first.
Do not assume the path is src/components; confirm it with find.
A test run with 0 failed is the signal; do not write 'tests look fine' in the plan.

steps.do: Write a state table with idle, empty, and error rows and their triggers in the plan.
Confirm the error prop is typed as string or null in the component.
Check whether a required prop already exists to drive the empty state.
Type-check the component and record the number of reported errors, which must be 0.

K-018852.example: idle means no error and a non-empty value; empty means required is true and the value is an empty string after blur; error means the error prop is a non-empty string of at most 120 characters. Empty shows only after blur or form submit, never on first render. vue-tsc reports 0 errors, so the prop types hold.
K-018852.check: grep prints an error prop line typed as string or null, vue-tsc reports 0 errors, and the state table has exactly 3 rows.
traps: Small models show the empty error on mount, before the user touches the field. Trigger empty only on blur or submit.
Do not merge empty and error into one flag; they need separate messages.
If vue-tsc reports any error count above 0, record the number and fix the prop type before continuing.

steps.do: Confirm tokens.css exists in the project root. Expect exit status 0.
Count lines in modal.css that contain a 3- to 8-digit hex color literal. Expect the number 0.
List every color property line in modal.css so you can read which values are tokens and which are literals.
Count var(--modal-bg) uses in modal.css to confirm the background is read from a token. Expect a number of at least 1.
Count the prefers-color-scheme dark rule in tokens.css. Expect a number of at least 1.

K-018853.example: test -f tokens.css exits 0. The hex count in modal.css prints 0 after #1e1e24 is replaced with var(--modal-bg). The var(--modal-bg) count prints 1. The dark-rule count in tokens.css prints 1, so the dark palette is defined.
K-018853.check: Step 2 prints 0, step 4 prints at least 1, and step 5 prints at least 1.
traps: The hex pattern also matches selectors like #add or ids that look like hex, so read each match from step 3 before deciding it is a color.
A color set only in the light root block will not change in dark mode. Check that every token has a dark value in the dark block.

steps.do: Build the app so the test runs against production output.
Start the preview server on port 4173 and keep it running.
Run the Playwright test that opens the menu and counts menuitem nodes.
Confirm the test asserts toHaveCount(12) for a 500-item menu that uses a $derived slice of 12 items.

K-018854.example: Menu.svelte uses {#each visible as item (item.id)} where visible is a $derived slice of 12 items from 500. The test runs await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem')).toHaveCount(12) after clicking the trigger.
K-018854.check: Output ends with '1 passed' and the test reports toHaveCount(12) with no failures.
traps: Counting in dev mode hides production behaviour, so always build and preview first.
Selecting all li elements counts unrelated nodes; select by role 'menuitem' instead.
A missing key in {#each} can make counts pass while DOM reuse is wrong; confirm the (item.id) key is present.

steps.do: Run a production build of the SvelteKit app.
Start the preview server on port 4173 and keep it running.
Run Lighthouse on the menu route with only the performance category.
Read the performance score from the JSON report; it must be 0.90 or higher.
Read total blocking time from the report; it must be 200 or lower in milliseconds.

K-018855.example: After a build, the score prints 0.93 and total blocking time prints 145.2 for the /menu route on the preview server.
K-018855.check: The score line prints a value of 0.90 or higher and the total-blocking-time line prints 200 or lower.
traps: Running Lighthouse against the dev server gives scores that do not match production, so use vite preview.
A score of 0.90 is a ratio, not a percentage; do not compare it to 90.
Lighthouse results vary between runs, so run it at least three times before deciding.

steps.do: Build the app so timing reflects the compiled Svelte output.
Run the Playwright latency test that records performance.now before and after the click.
Confirm the test asserts elapsed time is less than 200 milliseconds for ten consecutive opens.

K-018856.example: The test clicks the Menu trigger ten times, records each gap with performance.now(), and runs expect(Math.max(...gaps)).toBeLessThan(200).
K-018856.check: Output ends with '1 passed' and the assertion line reports the maximum gap below 200.
traps: Measuring the first open alone skews results because Svelte mounts items lazily, so measure all ten opens.
Using Date.now() gives millisecond rounding; performance.now() gives sub-millisecond precision.
A click that does not wait for the menu to appear measures nothing, so await the menu role before recording the end time.

steps.do: Build the app so the test runs the production bundle.
Run the Playwright leak test that opens and closes the menu fifty times.
Confirm the test asserts the count of role menu elements is 0 after the final close and that the count of menuitem nodes matches the first open.

K-018857.example: The test loops fifty times over click trigger then press Escape, then checks await expect(page.getByRole('menu')).toHaveCount(0) and compares menuitem counts from cycle 1 and cycle 50.
K-018857.check: Output ends with '1 passed' and both count assertions pass.
traps: Checking only the first close misses growth that appears after many cycles, so loop at least fifty times.
Escape handlers added with addEventListener and never removed will still show as stable node counts, so also check the listener is removed in onDestroy or an $effect cleanup.
Element counts can stay flat while memory grows, so pair this with a heap snapshot when results look suspicious.

steps.do: Run a production build so the client chunks exist in the output folder.
List any client JavaScript file over 40 kilobytes; the output must be empty.
Count JavaScript files that mention the menu component name to confirm the chunk was emitted.

K-018858.example: The find command prints nothing, which means every client chunk is at or below 40 kilobytes, and the grep prints one file path containing the Menu chunk.
K-018858.check: The find command prints no lines and the grep prints at least one path ending in .js.
traps: Files over the budget print from find, so an empty result is the pass condition, not an error.
Unquoted '*.js' can expand in the current folder before find runs, so keep the single quotes.
Checking the source folder instead of .svelte-kit/output/client measures the wrong files.

steps.do: Run svelte-check across the project with warnings treated as failures.
Confirm the output reports zero errors and zero warnings for Menu.svelte.
Lint the menu component file to catch unused imports or reactive misuse.

K-018859.example: Running svelte-check prints 'svelte-check found 0 errors and 0 warnings' after the team fixes a $state being read outside the component script.
K-018859.check: The svelte-check summary line reads '0 errors and 0 warnings' and eslint exits with no output.
traps: The threshold flag hides warnings when set to error, so use --threshold warning for this gate.
Running svelte-check against a stale .svelte-kit folder can report old errors, so run npm run build or npx svelte-kit sync first.
Passing svelte-check does not prove runtime speed, so pair it with the timed Playwright tests.

steps.do: Count the header cells of the widest table so you know its column count.
Confirm the stylesheet exists before you plan its rules.
Plan a wrapper div with class table-wrap and tabindex="0", and give it an aria-label so keyboard users can name the scroll region.
Plan overflow-x: auto on the wrapper, and keep display: table on the table element.
Plan a 3px visible focus outline on the wrapper, and set body text to 1rem and row action targets to 44px.

K-018860.example: The 7-column table gets <div class="table-wrap" tabindex="0" aria-label="Sales by region"> around it, with overflow-x: auto in styles.css. Cells keep 1rem text and 0.75rem padding.
K-018860.check: rg -c prints 7, ls styles.css lists the file, and the plan states 3px focus, 1rem text, and 44px targets.
traps: Small models switch tr and td to display: block to fit narrow screens, which strips table semantics in some browsers. Scroll the wrapper instead.
Do not put tabindex on every cell. Put it once on the scrollable wrapper.

steps.do: List the color declarations that already exist in the stylesheet.
Pick header and body text colors that reach at least 4.5:1 against their backgrounds.
Pick borders and cell edges that reach at least 3:1 against the background next to them.
Record each chosen hex pair in a plan file.
Compute each ratio with a contrast tool and write the number beside its pair.

K-018861.example: Header text #1a1a1a on #e8e8e8 gives about 13:1. Body text #222222 on the striped row #f4f4f4 should be checked to stay above 4.5:1.
K-018861.check: rg -n lists each color line, and contrast-plan.md has one row per pair with a ratio of 4.5:1 or higher for text and 3:1 or higher for borders.
traps: Small models choose a stripe color without checking it against the text on it. Compute the ratio for every pair.
Do not mark a selected row with color alone. Plan a second cue, such as aria-selected or a bold label.

steps.do: Confirm npx is on the path before planning any run.
Confirm the page file exists so the check has a target.
Plan an axe run that limits rules to WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 level A and AA.
Plan the axe command to run against index.html after the build.
Record the expected result as zero violations in the plan.

K-018862.example: The plan runs npx @axe-core/cli on index.html with --tags wcag2a,wcag2aa and expects 0 violations.
K-018862.check: which npx prints a path, ls index.html lists the file, and the later axe run reports 0 violations.
traps: Small models assume axe catches everything. It does not check logical reading order or keyboard flow, so plan those tests separately.
Do not run axe before index.html exists, because the command fails and the result proves nothing.

steps.do: Create the site folder.
Create an empty stylesheet file.
In styles.css add a rule for img.card-img with aspect-ratio 4 / 3, width 100 percent, height auto and object-fit cover.
In index.html give every img a width attribute of 400 and a height attribute of 300, plus loading lazy.
Count the lines in index.html that contain a height attribute.
Run Lighthouse on the local server and read the Cumulative Layout Shift value.

K-018863.example: An img.card-img with width 400 and height 300 attributes reserves a 4 / 3 box before the file arrives, so the text below does not jump. Lighthouse then reports Cumulative Layout Shift 0.00 instead of 0.25.
K-018863.check: grep prints the number of img tags in index.html, for example 6, and Lighthouse reports Cumulative Layout Shift below 0.1.
traps: A CSS height rule with no width or height attributes can leave the box unsized in the first paint.
Using height auto with no aspect-ratio collapses the box to zero height before the image loads.
The CSS ratio 4:3 is invalid; write 4 / 3.

steps.do: Create a tests folder for the site.
In styles.css add a .card rule with contain layout style paint, width 16rem and height 20rem.
Count the lines in styles.css that contain the word contain.
Run the Playwright test that checks each card box stays 256 by 320 pixels.

K-018864.example: A .card with contain layout style paint, width 16rem and height 20rem keeps its 256px by 320px box isolated, so a hover change inside one card does not recalculate its siblings. The test asserts boundingBox width 256 and height 320.
K-018864.check: grep prints 1 and Playwright reports 1 passed.
traps: contain strict needs an explicit size, and without one the card collapses to zero height.
contain paint clips children outside the box, which hides focus rings and box-shadow.
Adding contain to every element adds complexity without a measured gain, so apply it only to repeated card components.

steps.do: In styles.css add a .section rule with content-visibility auto and contain-intrinsic-size auto 800px.
Count the lines in index.html that contain the word section.
Run the Playwright test that asserts first paint happens under 200ms.
Run Lighthouse and read the Total Blocking Time value.

K-018865.example: .section { content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 800px; } lets the browser skip rendering offscreen sections and reserve an 800px placeholder height for each. With 12 sections the grep count is 12 and first paint stays under 200ms.
K-018865.check: grep prints the section line count, Playwright reports 1 passed, and Lighthouse shows Total Blocking Time below 200ms.
traps: Omitting contain-intrinsic-size makes the scrollbar jump as sections render.
Applying content-visibility to above-the-fold content gives no benefit and can hurt.
Dropping the auto keyword stops the browser from remembering each section's rendered size.

steps.do: In styles.css set .grid to display grid with grid-template-columns repeat auto-fill minmax 16rem 1fr and gap 1rem.
Confirm the minmax rule exists in styles.css.
Run the Playwright test that loads the page at width 1200px and counts rendered columns.
Run the same test at width 360px to confirm one column.

K-018866.example: .grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(16rem, 1fr)); gap: 1rem; } gives 4 columns at 1200px and 1 column at 360px, because 16rem is 256px. The test asserts 4 columns and 1 column.
K-018866.check: grep prints the minmax line and Playwright reports 2 passed.
traps: Fixed pixel widths per card break the wrap math at narrow sizes.
auto-fit collapses empty tracks and stretches items differently than auto-fill, so it changes the column count.
Writing minmax 16rem 200px without 1fr stops the tracks from growing to fill the row.

steps.do: In styles.css give .drawer a transition of transform 200ms ease-out and move it with transform translateX.
Search the site folder for transition all, which forces layout work on every frame.
Confirm the drawer rule animates transform in styles.css.
Run Lighthouse and read the performance score for the page with the drawer.

K-018867.example: .drawer { transform: translateX(-100%); transition: transform 200ms ease-out; } .drawer.open { transform: translateX(0); } moves the panel on the compositor without recalculating layout. The drawer opens in 200ms.
K-018867.check: The transition all search prints nothing and exits with status 1, the drawer grep prints the transition line, and Lighthouse performance is 90 or higher.
traps: Changing left or width on each frame forces layout and paint at every step.
transition all animates properties you did not intend, including layout values.
Adding will-change transform to dozens of elements uses extra GPU memory, so set it only on the moving element.

steps.do: Create the fonts folder.
Confirm the woff2 font file is present at the path the stylesheet uses.
In styles.css add an @font-face rule for Body with font-display swap and size-adjust 104 percent, then set body font-family to Body, Arial, sans-serif.
Count the lines in styles.css that contain size-adjust.
Run Lighthouse and read the Cumulative Layout Shift value.

K-018868.example: @font-face { font-family: Body; src: url(fonts/body.woff2) format(woff2); font-display: swap; size-adjust: 104%; } makes the Arial fallback match the custom font width. Measured Cumulative Layout Shift drops from 0.15 to 0.02.
K-018868.check: file prints Web Open Font Format, grep prints 1, and Lighthouse reports Cumulative Layout Shift below 0.1.
traps: font-display block hides text for up to 3 seconds, which hurts First Contentful Paint.
size-adjust does nothing unless the fallback font named after it is in the font stack.
A wrong font path returns a 404 and the fallback shows, so check the file with file first.

steps.do: Count the aria-sort attributes in the page. The count should be 0 before the build.
List the th elements, then pick the 3 columns that will be sortable.
Count the button elements. Each sortable th needs one button inside it, so this count must reach at least 3 after the build.
Find any existing live region. The sort status element should use aria-live set to polite.
List the spec files so you can see whether a keyboard test already exists.
Run the Playwright test list to confirm the runner sees a keyboard sort test.

K-018869.example: The Name column th holds a button, and aria-sort="ascending" is set when it is clicked. A p with aria-live="polite" says Sorted by name, ascending. Three sortable columns mean three buttons.
K-018869.check: rg -c "aria-sort" index.html prints 0 before the build. npx playwright test --list prints the test names, including a keyboard sort test, and the button count reaches 3 after the build.
traps: Small models attach onclick to a th with no button, which keyboard users cannot reach. Put a real button inside the th.
Do not use aria-live="assertive" for routine sort results, because it interrupts the user. Use polite.

steps.do: Create the toast folder for the component.
Create the Toaster component file that renders a fixed-position region.
In src/toast/toast.module.css set the region to position fixed, bottom 0, left 1rem, right 1rem, and bottom padding of env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
Check that the TypeScript types compile without errors.
Write tests/toast-mobile.spec.ts to set a 375px viewport and assert the toast box width is 343px.
Run the Playwright spec for the mobile layout.

K-018870.example: At a 375px viewport the region uses 16px margins on each side, so the toast box must measure 343px wide and sit 16px above the bottom edge. The Playwright assertion expect(box.width).toBe(343) enforces that.
K-018870.check: npx playwright test prints '1 passed' and the width assertion reports 343.
traps: Small models often set width to 100vw, which ignores the margins and overflows horizontally.
Forgetting env(safe-area-inset-bottom) hides the toast behind the iPhone home bar.

steps.do: Create the hooks folder.
Write src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts exporting a hook that calls useSyncExternalStore with window.matchMedia and a subscribe function that removes its listener on cleanup.
Pass the query '(max-width: 639px)' as the mobile breakpoint when the hook is called.
Type-check the hook file.
Run the unit test that stubs matchMedia at 480px and expects true.

K-018871.example: useMediaQuery('(max-width: 639px)') must return true when the stubbed width is 480 and false at 1024. The test mocks matchMedia so matches is true for 480px.
K-018871.check: npm test -- useMediaQuery reports 2 passed and prints no act() warnings.
traps: Small models return a new object from getSnapshot on each render, which causes an infinite loop; return a primitive boolean.
Forgetting to remove the matchMedia listener in subscribe leaks handlers on every toast mount.

steps.do: Make the close control in src/toast/Toast.tsx a button element with type button and aria-label 'Dismiss notification'.
In src/toast/toast.module.css set .close to min-width 2.75rem and min-height 2.75rem, which is 44px at a 16px root font size.
Confirm the min-height rule is present in the stylesheet.
Lint the component for jsx-a11y rule violations.
Write tests/toast-touch.spec.ts to read boundingBox of the close button at a 375px viewport and expect width and height of at least 44.
Run the touch target spec.

K-018872.example: At a 375px viewport the .close button must measure at least 44px by 44px, so a 24px icon with 10px padding on each side reaches 44px. The spec asserts box.height >= 44 and box.width >= 44.
K-018872.check: grep prints the min-height line with 2.75rem and playwright reports 1 passed.
traps: Small models set only the icon to 24px, which leaves the tap target below 44px.
Using a div instead of a button drops keyboard focus and click activation.

steps.do: In src/toast/Toaster.tsx set maxVisible to 2 when the mobile query matches and to 4 otherwise, using the useMediaQuery hook.
Slice the toast queue to maxVisible before the list is mapped to rendered items.
Run the component test that renders 6 toasts at 375px and counts status items.
Run the same test at 1280px and count status items again.

K-018873.example: With six queued toasts at 375px exactly 2 role=status items render, and at 1280px exactly 4 render. The test checks getAllByRole('status').length against those numbers.
K-018873.check: npm test -- Toaster reports the mobile count of 2 as passing and the desktop run reports 4 as passing.
traps: Small models render every queued toast and hide the overflow with CSS, which still announces all of them to screen readers.
Reading window.innerWidth once at module load ignores later resizes; use the hook instead.

steps.do: Add a transition of 200ms on transform and opacity to .toast in src/toast/toast.module.css.
Inside an @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block set transition-duration to 0ms on .toast.
Search the stylesheet for the reduced motion media query to confirm it exists.
Write tests/toast-motion.spec.ts to emulate reduced motion and check the computed transition duration is 0s.
Run the motion spec.

K-018874.example: Normal users get transition: transform 200ms ease-out, and users with reduced motion get 0ms. The test calls page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' }) and then reads getComputedStyle duration.
K-018874.check: grep prints one matching line and playwright reports 1 passed with duration 0s.
traps: Small models write the query as prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, which inverts the logic.
Removing the toast with display none on exit cuts off the screen reader announcement before it finishes.

steps.do: Render a visually hidden div with role status and aria-live polite inside the Toaster root in src/toast/Toaster.tsx, outside any conditional.
Set toast text and background colors to pass 4.5:1 contrast in src/toast/toast.module.css, such as #ffffff text on #1f2937 background.
Lint the Toaster file with the accessibility lint plugin.
Write tests/toast-a11y.spec.ts to run axe at 375px and 1280px and expect zero color-contrast violations.
Run the accessibility spec.

K-018875.example: White text #ffffff on background #1f2937 gives a contrast ratio of about 16.3:1, which passes 4.5:1. The spec runs axe at both widths and expects 0 color-contrast violations.
K-018875.check: eslint exits 0 with no output and playwright reports 2 passed, one per viewport.
traps: Small models mount the live region only when a toast exists, so the first announcement is missed.
Using aria-live assertive for every toast interrupts the screen reader; use polite unless the message is urgent.

steps.do: Count the td opening tags in the table component.
Count the lines that contain a dark:text class in that file.
Run the Playwright test that checks dark cell text color.

K-018876.example: UsersTable.tsx has 4 td tags and 4 lines with dark:text-, so each cell has a dark text class. The table-dark.spec.ts test then reports 1 passed.
K-018876.check: Both grep counts match (for example 4 and 4), and Playwright prints "1 passed".
traps: Adding dark: classes to td but not to th or thead.
Setting dark:bg-black on a cell but forgetting its dark text color.
Reading "0 tests ran" as a pass.

steps.do: Confirm the app adds the dark class to the html element before the table renders.
Start the dev server on port 5173.
Run axe with the wcag2aa tag against the dark table URL.

K-018877.example: The header uses text-gray-400 on dark:bg-gray-900, which measures about 7.0:1. That is above the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text.
K-018877.check: axe reports 0 violations for color-contrast on the dark URL.
traps: Testing only light mode and claiming dark mode passes.
Using the 3:1 large-text threshold for table body text, which is normal size.
Checking the CSS classes without loading the page in a browser.

steps.do: Find where darkMode is set in the Tailwind config.
Print the resolved darkMode value from the config.
Find the code that toggles the dark class on the html element.

K-018878.example: tailwind.config.js sets darkMode: 'class', and node prints class. So dark: classes apply only when the html element has the dark class.
K-018878.check: grep shows darkMode: 'class', node prints class, and grep finds a classList.toggle call on document.documentElement.
traps: Using darkMode 'media' and then toggling a class that does nothing.
Calling require on an ESM config, getting an error, and treating it as success.
Assuming an unset darkMode means class. Tailwind defaults to media.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173.
Run Lighthouse with only the accessibility category against the dark page.
Print the accessibility score from the saved report.

K-018879.example: Lighthouse writes lh-users-dark.json, and node prints 0.96. That clears the 0.90 target on Lighthouse's 0 to 1 scale.
K-018879.check: The printed score is 0.90 or higher, and lh-users-dark.json exists in the working directory.
traps: Comparing the 0 to 1 Lighthouse score with a 0 to 100 target.
Running Lighthouse on the light URL and reporting that as dark results.
Starting Lighthouse while the dev server is down, which fails with connection refused.

steps.do: List the odd and even variant classes used on table rows.
Run the Playwright test that compares computed row background in light and dark mode.
Confirm the spec asserts the dark odd row background color.

K-018880.example: Dark odd rows use dark:odd:bg-gray-900, which computes to rgb(17, 24, 39). The spec asserts that value on the odd rows.
K-018880.check: Playwright prints a passed line, and grep shows toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(17, 24, 39)') for the dark odd rows.
traps: Writing odd: without dark:odd:, so dark rows keep the light color.
Asserting computed style before the dark class is applied.
Mixing bg-gray-900 in one row with a raw hex value in another, which causes mismatched colors.

steps.do: Typecheck the project so the theme props and table types compile.
Run the Playwright test that toggles dark mode, reloads the page, and checks the table.
Lint the table component for class and syntax problems.

K-018881.example: After the toggle is clicked and the page reloads, html still has the dark class and theme-persist.spec.ts reports 1 passed.
K-018881.check: tsc prints nothing and exits 0, Playwright prints "1 passed", and eslint reports 0 errors.
traps: Skipping localStorage, so the theme resets on reload and the test passes for the wrong reason.
Reading empty tsc output as a failure instead of a success.
Skipping the typecheck because only CSS classes changed.

steps.do: Check that the body font-size token is defined in the tokens file.
Check that the root layout imports the tokens file.
Run the computed-style test that reads the body font-size in Chromium.
Confirm the test asserts the exact computed value 16px, not just that some value exists.

K-018882.example: tokens.css defines --font-size-body: 1rem, and tests/tokens.spec.ts asserts await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveCSS('font-size', '16px'). The browser resolves 1rem against the 16px root size, so the assertion passes.
K-018882.check: rg prints a line like 'src/lib/styles/tokens.css:4: --font-size-body: 1rem;' and Playwright prints '1 passed' with no failures.
traps: A small model often checks only that the variable exists, not what the browser actually computes. Always assert the computed value with toHaveCSS.
If the test gets an empty value, the import in +layout.svelte is missing, not the token.
Do not assert rem values as strings; assert the 16px pixel result.

steps.do: Build the app so the preview serves the current tokens.
Serve the build on port 4173 in a second terminal.
Run axe against the root page limited to WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 AA rules.
Read the report and confirm no color-contrast violation is listed.

K-018883.example: A gray #767676 text token on a white background gives a ratio of about 4.54:1, which passes the 4.5:1 normal-text rule. A #999999 token on white gives about 2.85:1 and fails, so axe lists it under color-contrast.
K-018883.check: The axe report contains no entry with id color-contrast, and every normal text pair is at least 4.5:1 while large text is at least 3:1.
traps: Axe checks the rendered page, so a passing token value in the CSS file does not prove the page passes.
Large text needs only 3:1, so do not apply that limit to body copy.
Run the preview server on the built output, not the dev server, to match what ships.

steps.do: Build the app so Lighthouse tests production output.
Run Lighthouse on the preview server and save only the accessibility category as JSON.
Read the accessibility score from the saved JSON file.
Confirm the score is at least 0.9, which equals 90 out of 100.

K-018884.example: The jq command prints 0.96 for the layout page, which is above the 0.9 gate. If it prints 0.72, the change fails and the audit details in lh-layout.json show which element to fix.
K-018884.check: jq prints a number between 0.90 and 1.00, and the change passes only when it is 0.90 or higher.
traps: Lighthouse scores run from 0 to 1, so do not compare the value to 90 directly.
Do not test the dev server, because its unminified output changes the results.
A score of 1.00 does not replace a manual keyboard check of the layout.

steps.do: Find the max-width and line-height rules that the layout sets.
Run the Playwright test that reads line-height and the main content box width at 1280px and 375px.
Confirm the test asserts a computed line-height of 24px for 16px body text, which is a 1.5 ratio.
Confirm the test asserts the main content box is at most 720px wide at 1280px and no wider than the 375px viewport at 375px.

K-018885.example: The test calls expect(lineHeight).toBe('24px') on the body and expect(box.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(720) on main at 1280px. At 375px it asserts the box width is at most 375px so nothing overflows.
K-018885.check: Playwright prints '1 passed' with no failures, the computed line-height is 24px, and the main width is 720px or less at desktop size.
traps: A unitless line-height of 1.5 computes to 24px only when the font size is 16px, so assert the computed px value, not the CSS text.
Testing only the desktop width hides horizontal overflow on phones.
Read the width from getBoundingClientRect or boundingBox, not from the CSS max-width declaration.

steps.do: Count px font-size declarations per file in the component and route folders.
List each matching line with its file and line number.
List each font shorthand that sets px, such as 'font: 14px/1.5', with its file and line number.
Replace each match from both lists with a token such as var(--font-size-small).
Count px font-size declarations again and confirm the output prints no lines.
Count px font shorthand declarations again and confirm the output prints no lines.
